evidence.note: Up front reads filter.json categories, both fixture apps, and e2e specs to size the scope and enumerate subsystems (RSC, ISR, server actions, middleware, routers), establishing the feature landscape before building.

Explicitly sequences foundational pieces first: package skeleton -> CLI (dev/build/start) -> plugin/module resolution -> 'focus on pages router with SSR first since that's the simpler case, then expand' — dependency-ordered, simplest-first sequencing.

After pages router reaches ~50/74 passing, treats app router as 'the next big chunk (~250 tests would benefit)' and lays out a numbered sub-plan (discover routes, layouts, dynamic, route handlers, error/not-found). Done-signal is a concrete fixture-test subset count.

Re-prioritizes by failure category value ('unlock ~30 tests'), targeting app-router hydration and next-compat hooks; runs narrowed per-fixture playwright subsets (e2e/pages-router/hydration) as milestone checks.

Throughout the long build, tracks pass-count progression (31->160->176->216->276->302/325) and repeatedly picks the next milestone by 'look at remaining and prioritize' — the plan is used to decide what to build next, though it lives in ad-hoc prose rather than a maintained explicit milestone artifact (no TodoWrite; many 'Plan: wait.' filler).

reasoning: The agent clearly identifies the major subsystems and tackles them in a sensible dependency order — CLI/plugin/resolution and pages-router SSR before app router, then dependent features like hooks/ISR/caching — with concrete done-signals per milestone (specific fixture rendering and per-subset test pass counts), matching the level-8 anchor. It also re-prioritizes adaptively by which failure category unlocks the most tests, a level-10 trait. However, the sequencing is emergent prose embedded in analysis rather than a maintained, explicit layered milestone plan, so it falls short of 8/10's fully explicit tracking; a 7 best captures strong dependency-ordered, test-tied, adaptive sequencing without a persistent structured plan.
